title: Edge cluster driver compatibility sanity draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a sanity-focused compatibility matrix and validation playbook for small/edge Kubernetes clusters that run GPUs in VPC/on-prem private deployments. Aim: reduce risk for rolling driver/CUDA/NCCL upgrades, outline fast smoke tests, and document a minimal rollback path if a node or pod fleet shows regressions.

Scope and context:
- Target clusters: 3-12 node edge clusters with mixed GPU types (A10/L4/A100 as encountered).
- Deploy model: kubeadm managed K8s (1.26–1.28), containerd runtime, Calico CNI, private registry.
- Infrastructure managed by terraform modules: tf-mod-vpc-edge (networking), tf-mod-gpu-k8s (node pools), tf-mod-ssh-agent (bastion).
- This doc is intentionally lightweight: quick checks for validators (SRE/Infra on-call) and template commands for CI sanity jobs.

Quick decision matrix (sanity-first):
NOTE: rows are combinations we ran in the lab. "OK" means basic inference containers (LLM runtime toy workloads) launched and ran short-token generation w/o GPU OOMs or kernel crashes.

K8s  | Driver (runfile) | CUDA | NCCL | GPU models tested | Result | Notes
1.26 | 535.104         | 12.2 | 2.16 | A10, L4          | OK     | minor warnings in kernel dmesg on L4 with 535.104; acceptable for canary
1.27 | 540.21         | 12.3 | 2.18 | A10, A100        | OK     | A100 needs nvidia-container-toolkit 1.11+
1.28 | 545.40         | 12.4 | 2.20 | A100             | FAIL   | observed nvidia-uvm module crash after long tail requests (reproducible)
1.27 | 535.104         | 12.2 | 2.16 | L4               | WARN   | throttling observed under synthetic load

Lab validation notes (short):
- 1.28 + driver 545.40: reproduction steps attached; root cause seems tied to 545.x driver + kernel 5.15 combination used in our edge images. Filed JIRA INFRA-1023.
- L4-specific thermal throttling happens when pods schedule with heavy continuous decode loops; mitigated by cgroup+gpu-plugin knob limiting MIG slices.
- NCCL 2.20 used for A100 multi-GPU tests; fine for intra-node comms but we still avoid enabling inter-node NCCL for edge due to flaky network MTU.

Validation checklist (manual/CI both):
1) Pre-upgrade
   - snapshot node images: tar/gz of /var/lib/… and index of installed packages (rpm/dpkg).
   - taint a small percentage of nodes for canary (use tf-mod tags to target a small nodepool).
   - create a reproducible smoke job (small container: ubuntu + nvidia/cuda:12.2 + mini LLM inference script).
2) Upgrade step
   - drain target node (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).
   - install driver via runfile with --silent and record install log (/var/log/nvidia-install-YYYYMMDD.log).
   - update node image tag in tf-mod-gpu-k8s if image-baked drivers used, otherwise update cloud-init to install X.
   - uncordon and run smoke job against node (label-based scheduler).
3) Post-upgrade validation (5–30m window)
   - kubectl describe node -> check for nvidia.com/gpu allocatable and device plugin ready.
   - docker/containerd logs for nvidia-container-runtime errors.
   - dmesg tail for nvidia/uvm/panic lines.
   - run token-gen job for 5 loops; assert not exceeding baseline latency p50 by >2x.
   - check coredumps (journalctl -u kubelet & /var/crash).

Smoke test script (CI-friendly, pseudocode):
- docker run --gpus all --rm
  -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 nvidia/cuda:12.2-base npx node mini-llm.js --tokens 64 --seed 42
- success criteria: exit 0 + stdout contains "generation complete" + gpu-util > 2% during run

Rollback primitives (fast path):
- If driver install fails or nodes start OOMing/kernel crashing: immediate plan is to cordon+drain affected nodes and rotate to previous nodepool that has the known-good driver (tf-mod creates alpha/beta nodepools).
- If nodes were in-place-upgraded, revert by booting into previous VM image snapshot or reinstall previous driver runfile (logged installer path matters).
- For fleets with mixed GPUs, prefer to demote suspect nodepool via taints to avoid scheduler placing new pods there.
- Urgent: disable any aggressive autoscaler policies that would place new pods on affected nodes until validated.

Terraform notes (module-focused):
- tf-mod-gpu-k8s: add new variable driver_install_mode = ["image-baked", "cloud-init", "daemonset-runfile"], default "daemonset-runfile" for edge clusters.
- tf-mod-vpc-edge: include an output bastion_ssh_keys for quick node image rollbacks; store snapshots id as tags for automation.
- plan: a small helper script tf/upgrade-driver.sh that: updates module var, applies to create canary nodepool, waits for node readiness, triggers CI smoke and promotes. Keep that script idempotent.

Known gotchas and heuristics:
- Kubelet versions below 1.26 sometimes show device-plugin reconcilers race after rapid driver reinstall; add 30s sleep between unloading uvm and reinstall steps.
- containerd older than 1.6 needs nvidia-container-runtime-hook 1.x compatibility check.
- Kernel mismatch: drivers in 545.x show regressions on kernel 5.15 in our images; prefer 540.x on 5.15 or upgrade kernel to 5.19+ for 545.x.
- NCCL multi-node is brittle on network MTU != 1500; for edge clusters set MTU explicitly in Calico and test with iperf.

Lightweight test results (latest run 2026-01-15):
- Canary set: 3 nodes (A10 x2, L4 x1), kube 1.27, driver 540.21, cuda 12.3, nccl 2.18 -> PASS (3/3)
- Canary set: 2 nodes (A100 x2), kube 1.28, driver 545.40, cuda 12.4, nccl 2.20 -> FAIL (0/2) - reproduced kernel panic

Action items (next):
- [ ] Finalize tf-mod change to create named nodepool groups (beta/gold) for safe rollouts. Owner: Marco
- [ ] Add CI job that runs the smoke test script against newly created canary pool. Owner: Lina
- [ ] Reproduce 545.40 kernel panic with different host kernel (5.19) to isolate kernel vs driver. Owner: Asha
- [ ] Draft runbook excerpt for on-call with 3-step rollback checklist and Slack playbook. Owner: Evan

Open questions:
- Should we pin containerd minimum in tf-mod to 1.6 for all edge clusters? Risk vs upgrade churn?
- Do we want to support in-place driver upgrades via DaemonSet or rely exclusively on image-baked nodes for edge? Pros/cons documented but need decision.

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Keep installer logs archived under s3://redwood-ops/driver-installs/<cluster>/<date>/installer.log
- If we change tf-mod, add acceptance test in infra pipeline so a PR triggers an ephemeral cluster with targeted driver/install-mode.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EDGE-GPU-COMPAT
- JIRA: INFRA-1023 (545.x kernel panic investigation)
- Github: github.com/redwood/tf-mod-gpu-k8s/pull/48 (proof-of-concept for nodepool promotion)

End of draft.

-- Asha
